273433369_45bcf7fc.text: The locus coeruleus (LC) region is divided into two parts: the LC, which primarily contains noradrenergic cells (NE, depicted in blue), and the peri-LC, which includes GABAergic neurons (depicted in grey). Within the noradrenergic cells, NE is synthesized through the conversion of Tyrosine (Tyr) to DOPA (3,4dihydroxyphenylalanine), then to Dopamine (DA), and finally to NE, which is released into the synaptic cleft. NE primarily acts on four types of receptors: α1, β1, β2, and α2 (an auto receptor). The degradation of NE occurs via the enzymes COMT (postsynaptic) and MAO-A (presynaptic) after reuptake by the NET transporter

273433369_78752938.text: .NE cells simultaneously secrete Galanin (GAL), Neuropeptide Y (NPY), and corticoliberine (CRF) acting on GAL1R, various NPY receptors (Y1, Y2, Y5), and CRF1R respectively. In mice, NPY is exclusively secreted by GABAergic cells in the peri-LC.
